title: Isolate a model by staging its inputs
statement: Give a reviewing or play-testing model a staged copy of its allowed inputs and nothing else, since an instruction or a read-only sandbox doesn't stop it reading more.
detail: An adversarial audit of a course-experience preflight rejected its first implementation partly because isolation was policy prose: read-only sandboxing prevented writes but did not stop reads of the host, the repository or sibling runs, and home-directory settings, absolute artifact paths and an ignore-rules flag weakened the boundary further. The audit rejected an instruction not to read other files as isolation, and the clean process must now receive a staged input directory and nothing else. A separate audit of a multi-agent review setup found that admitting evidence by filename or extension let another agent's memory, mailbox, transcript or secrets be copied into a worker's context under an unexpected name.

evidence.quote: 7. **Isolation was policy prose.** Read-only sandboxing prevented writes but did not stop host/repository/sibling reads. `HOME`, `CODEX_HOME`, absolute artifact paths, and `--ignore-rules` weakened the boundary.
The adversarial audit rejected “please do not read other files” as isolation. The clean process must receive a staged input directory and nothing else.

The evidence admission path used narrow filename/extension checks. Another agent's memory, full mailbox, transcript, or secret content under an unexpected filename could be copied into a worker context.
